case_name: JOSEPH KAIRAU v DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Conclusion: Corrections has not acted unjustifiably and Mr Kairau’s claim that the dismissal was unjustified is unsuccessful.
review_notes: Direct review of the serious-misconduct and process sections. The Authority found it reasonable for Corrections to conclude the conduct amounted to serious misconduct and found no process unfairness sufficient to invalidate dismissal.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedies; costs reserved.

case_name: YE LU v MANUKAU BUSES LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [43] I find that Mr Ye has a personal grievance for unjustifiable dismissal.
review_notes: Direct review of dismissal, process, contribution, remedies and counter-problem. Employer failed to investigate fairly or give Mr Ye a proper opportunity to respond.
remedies_awarded: $3,000 gross reimbursement; $15,000 compensation; employer counter-problem declined.

case_name: RZK v ALLIED SECURITY LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [24] Both sanctions imposed were substantively justified, including the conclusion that sleeping whilst working on site was serious misconduct that warranted dismissal. [27] All of RZK’s claims are dismissed.
review_notes: Direct and second source review of the disciplinary process and serious-misconduct finding.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedies; costs reserved.

case_name: CSN v ROYAL DISTRICT NURSING SERVICE NEW ZEALAND LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [92] CSN has an arguable case for unjustified dismissal ... [98] the interests of justice do not outweigh the balance of convenience ... Interim reinstatement application is declined.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Interim reinstatement only; substantive dismissal merits were expressly left for later determination.
column18: Interim application only; no final dismissal-merits remedy.

case_name: RASHEEL NAIDU v AZAK CARS LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [81] ACL is ordered to pay ... compensation ... of $6,300 for unjustified dismissal and lost wages of $8,636.06 gross.
review_notes: Direct and second source review of the dismissal finding, contribution and remedies.
remedies_awarded: $6,300 dismissal compensation; $8,636.06 gross lost wages; annual-leave arrears and filing fee.

case_name: DRE TAYLOR v MARK MANA
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [8] Mr Mana is ordered to pay Mr Taylor $2,321.56 as a contribution to his costs.
review_notes: Costs-only follow-up determination. It does not decide dismissal merits and must not duplicate the underlying merits decision.

case_name: SUSAN PRICE v PATHWAYS HEALTH LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [43] Ms Price should not be granted leave to raise the personal grievance out of time pursuant to s 114(4) and s 115 of the Act.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Timeliness/leave determination only; dismissal merits were not reached.
column18: No dismissal-merits remedy; costs awarded to respondent.

case_name: AJY v CHIEF EXCUTIVE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [202] Corrections unjustifiably disadvantaged and unjustifiably dismissed AJY.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. The Authority found dismissal unjustified and reduced compensation 20% for contributory conduct.
remedies_awarded: $24,000 compensation and $27,201.22 lost remuneration after contribution assessment.

case_name: MICHAEL SPICER v ALLIED SECURITY LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [68] Mr Spicer has not made out any of his grievance claim for unjustified dismissal or disadvantage or his claim to be paid for training.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. The alleged dismissal grievance failed on the merits of the casual-work relationship.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedies; costs reserved.

case_name: SHANE CLELAND v ATLAS CONCRETE LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [81] The employer’s actions overall resulted in the unjustified dismissal of Mr Cleland.
review_notes: Direct and second source review of the drug-test dismissal, process and s 124 contribution. Admitted cannabis use contributed but did not cure the employer’s failures.
remedies_awarded: $1,080 gross lost remuneration plus holiday pay; $12,000 compensation; wage arrears and interest.

case_name: FRANK MURRAY v WATERSHED LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [62] I do not find that Watershed Limited acted unjustifiably in the process followed or decisions made that led to the termination of Frank Murray’s employment.
review_notes: Direct and second source review of redundancy rationale, consultation and redeployment.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedies; costs reserved.

case_name: DARREN PYNE v INVACARE NEW ZEALAND LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Determination heading: Invacare New Zealand Limited acted unjustifiably in making its decision to dismiss Darren Pyne on the grounds of redundancy.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. The flaws went to the substance of the redundancy decision; compensation was reduced 15% for blameworthy conduct.
remedies_awarded: $27,500 lost remuneration and $8,500 compensation after contribution reduction.

case_name: JOHN ALLAN WILLIAMS v MITEK NEW ZEALAND LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: The Authority does not have jurisdiction to investigate Mr Williams’ claims ... because there is no employment relationship currently before the Authority.
review_notes: Jurisdiction determination only; the named respondent was not the employer and substantive dismissal merits were never reached.

case_name: NIANHUAI YU and YULAN LUO v JOE AND ZHOU LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [70] It has not been necessary for me to consider Mr Yu’s unjustified dismissal claim because it is time barred under s 114 of the Act.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Dismissal merits were expressly not considered because the grievance was time barred.
column18: Wage/holiday/penalty relief only; no dismissal-merits remedy.

case_name: DION HEARFIELD v BELLINGHAM MARINE NEW ZEALAND LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [52] The trial period clause ... was valid and effective ... The Authority had no jurisdiction to investigate whether the dismissal was substantively and procedurally justified.
review_notes: Valid trial-period jurisdiction bar. No dismissal-merits determination was made.

case_name: LESLEY MCBRIDE v THE ULITMATE CARE GROUP LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [70] These factors do not arise from breaches of duty by Ultimate Care so there is no basis for Ms McBride’s constructive dismissal claim. [71] Ms McBride’s claims are dismissed.
review_notes: Direct and second source review of constructive-dismissal causation and alleged employer breaches.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedies; costs reserved.

case_name: AJY v THE CHIEF EXECUTIVE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [6] AJY was the successful party ... the claim of unjustified dismissal [was found]. [11] Corrections is ordered to pay AJY $18,000 as a contribution to costs.
review_notes: Costs-only follow-up to 2022 NZERA 169. The underlying merits result is already counted there and this row must not duplicate it.

case_name: WEI WANG v ALLSTAR ROOFING LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [22] No application for leave was made ... Accordingly, the Authority did not further investigate a personal grievance claim for constructive dismissal.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Determination resolved disadvantage/wage claims; constructive-dismissal merits were not investigated.
column18: Wage/public-holiday relief, disadvantage compensation and penalty; no dismissal-merits remedy.

case_name: PAUL KING v ICE FIRE PROTECTION LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Outcome: Mr King’s unjustified constructive dismissal claim did not succeed.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Constructive-dismissal grievance expressly failed; separate COVID wage and medical-cost claims partly succeeded.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; separate $1,000 wage compensation and $115 medical reimbursement.

case_name: AMAR NATH v ADVANCED KITCHENS (NZ) LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: The determination records that an earlier determination found Mr Nath had established a personal grievance for unjustifiable constructive dismissal and awarded reimbursement of lost wages and compensatory damages; this determination addresses costs and instalments only.
review_notes: Costs/instalment follow-up to the separate merits decision 2022 NZERA 122. Excluded to avoid double counting.

case_name: KRP v FYM
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: The applicant’s personal grievance claim of unjustified disadvantage has been made out ... [90] reinstatement to the workplace is by consent.
review_notes: Unjustified-disadvantage/unpaid-leave determination, not a dismissal-merits decision. Employment remained extant and reinstatement was by consent.
column18: Salary arrears, KiwiSaver, $15,000 compensation and disbursement.

case_name: DAVID OSBORNE v CALLAGHAN INNOVATION
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Costs are reserved and will be dealt with once investigation into Mr Osborne’s substantive claims has been completed.
review_notes: Preliminary jurisdiction ruling on protected-disclosure pleadings. The substantive claims were expressly left to later investigation.

case_name: PENG WANG v BOTANY VEHICLE SERVICE 2004 LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [43] As a result Mr Wang had established a personal grievance for unjustified dismissal.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Employer failed fair disciplinary processes on two termination attempts; distress compensation reduced 10% for blameworthy conduct.
remedies_awarded: $2,880 lost wages and $13,500 compensation after contribution reduction.

case_name: KFL v CHIEF OF THE NEW ZEALAND DEFENCE FORCE
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [66] The following interim orders are made ... [67] Costs are reserved pending a final determination on the substantive matters.
review_notes: Interim medical-clearance/employment-investigation orders only. Substantive merits remained pending.

case_name: UNITE UNION First v AILINI ATI Second Applicant AND THE APPLICANTS NAMED IN SCHEDULE 1 Third to Thirteenth Applicants AND HOSPITALITY SERVICES LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [79] The personal grievances are therefore appropriately of the type, unjustified dismissal. [83] Each of the 12 applicant employees is entitled to compensation for having their employment terminated without justification.
review_notes: Direct and second source review of the collective redundancy/termination claims. No contributory conduct found.
remedies_awarded: Compensation to 12 dismissed employees; penalties reserved for later determination.

case_name: PEX v LYTTELTON PORT COMPANY LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [96] The breach of the Policy was serious misconduct and dismissal was appropriate ... [97] LPC’s dismissal of PEX was justified.
review_notes: Direct and second source review of two positive drug tests, serious misconduct and disciplinary process.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedies; claims dismissed.

case_name: CAROLE MARSHALL v ERIC FORSTER
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Ms Marshall’s resignation was caused by what Mr Forster did, so this is really a case of constructive dismissal ... and that dismissal was unjustified.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. No blameworthy contribution requiring reduction was found.
remedies_awarded: $2,500 lost wages and $10,000 compensation.

case_name: DAVID MORELLO v WASTE MANAGEMENT NZ LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Issues: Was Mr Morello unjustifiably disadvantaged by actions of WML with regard to the SPI payment? [28] Mr Morello’s claim is unsuccessful.
review_notes: Bonus/disadvantage dispute only. No dismissal grievance or dismissal-merits determination.

case_name: ALISON DANKS v PAK HOLDINGS LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [65] Having established her employment ended by way of an unjustified dismissal ... [72] compensation ... because of her unjustified dismissal.
review_notes: Direct and second source review of redundancy/constructive dismissal. No contributory conduct found.
remedies_awarded: $12,244.18 lost wages and $10,000 compensation.

case_name: MOHAMMED HANIF v ORORA PACKAGING NEW ZEALAND LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: The Authority found the employer unjustifiably disadvantaged Mr Hanif by suspending him and unjustifiably dismissed him on 5 March 2020.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Serious-misconduct grounds used for dismissal were not reasonably justified; no contributory reduction was made.
remedies_awarded: $28,000 global compensation for established personal grievances.

case_name: STEPHEN ELLIOT v BAY TROLLEYS LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [10] I ... dismiss the application for lack of prosecution. [11] For the above reasons, I dismiss Mr Elliot’s application.
review_notes: Procedural dismissal for non-prosecution, not an adjudication of employment-dismissal merits.

case_name: RUILIANG CHEN v JERRY KITCHEN & BATH LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: The first respondent is ordered to pay Mr Chen $10,000 ... for the humiliation, loss of dignity and injury to feelings he suffered as a result of his procedurally unjustified dismissal.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Dismissal was substantively justified but procedurally unjustified; blameworthy conduct was already reflected by denying lost remuneration, with no further s 124 reduction.
remedies_awarded: $10,000 distress compensation; no lost remuneration because substantive justification was established.

case_name: SAMUEL DAY v THE LAST WAVE LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [85] LW was both substantively and procedurally justified in dismissing Mr Day ... [86] Mr Day’s claim is dismissed.
review_notes: Direct and second source review of serious-misconduct allegations concerning service to intoxicated patrons and the disciplinary process.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedies; costs reserved.

case_name: BRUCE SMITH v RIGHT2DRIVE (NEW ZEALAND) LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Having found no breach there is no unjustified dismissal so it is not necessary to make any finding on any justification issues.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Constructive-dismissal grievance failed even though a separate good-faith breach/penalty was established.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; $4,000 good-faith penalty paid to Mr Smith.

case_name: CDK v LVQ
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [20] I grant an interim non-publication order until further order of the Authority.
review_notes: Interim non-publication determination only; no dismissal merits were decided.

case_name: WAIROA DISTRICT COUNCIL v SIMON MUTONHORI
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: These orders, while interim, shall remain in place until amended or lifted ... costs are best left till the substantive claims have been resolved.
review_notes: Interim orders pending substantive claims; no final dismissal-merits determination.

case_name: MAGDY MISHRIKI v THE FONO TRUST
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [52] Dr Mishriki was not an employee of the Clinic. It follows the Authority has no jurisdiction ... Dr Mishriki’s claim for unjustified dismissal therefore fails.
review_notes: Employment-status/jurisdiction determination. Dismissal merits were not reached because there was no employment relationship.

case_name: SUSAN BROWN v WATCHDOG SECURITY GROUP LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [82] Although the unjustified dismissal claim did not succeed ... [83] the evidence established an unjustified disadvantage grievance instead.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Dismissal grievance failed; separate disadvantage claim succeeded and is not used to change the binary dismissal result.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; $2,000 compensation for separate unjustified disadvantage.

case_name: PAULA SUNDIN v HELLOWORLD TRAVEL SERVICES (NZ) LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [33] Ms Sundin’s dismissal for redundancy on 29 October 2020 was unjustified. [34] Ms Sundin has established personal grievances for unjustified disadvantage and unjustified dismissal.
review_notes: Direct and second source review of redundancy rationale/process. No blameworthy contribution was found.
remedies_awarded: Three months lost remuneration at contractual salary plus compensation.

case_name: PRINCE DION COLLIER v MD CONSTRUCTION LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: A fair and reasonable employer could not have reached the conclusion that Mr Collier had committed serious misconduct ... Mr Collier has been successful in bringing his claim for an unjustified dismissal.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Serious-misconduct conclusion and covert-video process were unjustified; no contributory reduction.
remedies_awarded: Three months ordinary lost wages and $22,000 compensation.

case_name: DAVID COXHEAD v EASTERN INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [61] Mr Coxhead’s dismissal was a decision that EIT, as a fair and reasonable employer, could have reached in all the circumstances at the time. [62] Mr Coxhead’s claims are dismissed.
review_notes: Direct and second source review of summary dismissal for serious misconduct and the disciplinary process.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedies; costs reserved.

case_name: JOHN WILSON v TRANSPORT REFINISHERS LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Conclusion – constructive dismissal: I am satisfied the employer in this case has not breached its duties towards Mr Wilson ... I do not find these actions were a course of conduct with the dominant purpose of causing Mr Wilson to leave.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Constructive-dismissal grievance failed; remaining disadvantage/wage issues were separate.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy.

case_name: GLEN KEIGHRAN v KENSINGTON TAVERN LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [54] As it was not a constructive dismissal, Mr Keighran’s dismissal grievance does not succeed, because his employment ended due to his resignation and not as a result of dismissal.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Dismissal grievance failed; separate unjustified-disadvantage grievance succeeded.
remedies_awarded: No dismissal remedy; $5,000 compensation for separate unjustified disadvantage.

case_name: UNITE UNION First v AILINI ATI Second Applicant AND THE APPLICANTS NAMED IN SCHEDULE 1 Third to Thirteenth Applicants AND HOSPITALITY SERVICES LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: This follow-up fixes penalties after the earlier determination; the merits and compensation discussions were already resolved in 2022 NZERA 342.
review_notes: Penalty follow-up to 2022 NZERA 342. Excluded to avoid double counting the same 12 dismissal merits decisions.

case_name: HATSUE KOIZUMI v HONEYBUNCH PURE NATURALS NZ LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [20] Accordingly, the Authority finds that Ms Koizumi has a personal grievance of unjustifiable dismissal.
review_notes: Direct and second source review of the trial provision, dismissal, wage arrears and remedies.
remedies_awarded: $5,625 lost wages; $11,000 compensation; wage/holiday arrears, penalty, filing fee and costs.

case_name: CONNOR ROBERT SCOTT v TOPCATCH LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: The employer’s actions in terminating Mr Scott’s employment and the way in which it proceeded to reach that decision ... were not the actions of a fair and reasonable employer. Accordingly I find that Mr Scott has a personal grievance for unjustifiable dismissal.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Serious-misconduct dismissal was reached through an unjustifiable process; no blameworthy contribution found.
remedies_awarded: Dismissal compensation and other remedies ordered; costs reserved.

case_name: CAREY ROBINSON v PACT GROUP
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [46] The decision to dismiss Ms Robinson without notice for serious misconduct ... was not what a fair and reasonable employer could have done in all the circumstances. [47] Ms Robinson’s dismissal was unjustifiable.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Serious-misconduct allegations were not established and no contribution reduction was appropriate.
remedies_awarded: $20,000 compensation; lost-wage claim declined for mitigation reasons.

case_name: JUDITH SUBRITZKY v SLAVERING TUSK LIMITED (IN LIQUIDATION) t/a THE ROSE AND THISTLE INN
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: The breaches were serious. They went to the heart of the employment relationship and resulted in the applicant’s constructive dismissal.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Employer wage/employment-agreement breaches caused the constructive dismissal; director penalties were also determined.
remedies_awarded: Constructive-dismissal finding plus penalties/costs/disbursements against directors; employer in liquidation.

case_name: JACQUELINE FURNISS v WAIKANAE BEACH MOTEL LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: The dismissal for misconduct in relation to the Word document is not justified ... Orders include compensation because of her unjustified dismissal.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Dismissal was unjustified; remedies were reduced 25% for contributory conduct.
remedies_awarded: $11,864 lost wages and $15,000 compensation after 25% contribution reduction.

case_name: EVA POUROVA v IDEA SERVICES LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Issues: Was Ms Pourova unjustifiably disadvantaged in her employment? The determination concerns disciplinary investigation and a letter of expectations; dismissal was not being contemplated.
review_notes: Unjustified-disadvantage case only; employment continued and no dismissal merits were in issue.

case_name: KATIE WILLIAMS v SLAVERING TUSK LIMITED (IN LIQUIDATION) t/a THE ROSE AND THISTLE INN
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Ms Williams’ employment ended on 28 February 2019 as a result of her constructive dismissal ... the breaches went to the heart of the employment relationship and resulted in the applicant’s constructive dismissal.
review_notes: Direct and second source review. Repeated wage/agreement breaches caused constructive dismissal; director penalties were also determined.
remedies_awarded: Constructive-dismissal finding plus penalties/costs/disbursements against directors; employer in liquidation.

case_name: VINCENT BABE v SLD AGRICULTURE LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [72] Failure to pay Mr Babe his wages in full ... amounts to an unjustified disadvantage ... [87] orders concern wage, holiday, minimum-wage, compensation and costs.
review_notes: Wage-arrears/unjustified-disadvantage determination only. The text notes resignation but does not adjudicate a dismissal grievance.
column18: Wage/holiday/minimum-wage arrears, $5,000 disadvantage compensation and costs.

case_name: ROGER TEAGUE v PYROCLASSIC FIRES
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: [30] This conclusion means that Mr Teague’s substantive matter may proceed in the Authority. [31] In the interim, I order the parties to attend mediation.
review_notes: Preliminary determination only; substantive merits were expressly left to proceed later.

case_name: JIEPENG LI v NZ YOYO TRAVELLING LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Both jurisdiction grounds succeeded. The Authority agreed that it did not have jurisdiction to consider Mr Li’s dismissal grievance.
review_notes: Valid trial-period and timeliness jurisdiction bars; dismissal merits were not considered.
column18: Wage arrears, penalty and costs only.

case_name: JAMES PARTICK STEWART v AFFCO NEW ZEALAND LIMITED
supporting_quote_or_paragraph: Mr Stewart has established he has a personal grievance on the grounds AFFCO failed to include a provision that complies with s 67G of the Act in his employment agreement. His other claims fail.
review_notes: Employment-agreement/availability personal grievance only; no dismissal claim was decided.
